primitives.verbatim_quote: ## What Not To Do - Do not copy Unkey source into GSE.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B(t): [0,C]': 'Tokens remaining at time t', 'C: N': 'Bucket capacity (requests)', '\\lambda: [0,1]': 'Token fill rate (per second)', '1_{request}: 1': 'Indicator for request arrival'}
primitives.assumptions: Requests arrive independently, bucket resets on overflow, λ is constant.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Throttling triggers when B(t) < 0, causing queue buildup or rejection.

layer2.mapping: GSE implements leaky bucket variants for RPC rate control. GSI uses this for provider SLA enforcement.

Unkey's primitives formalize this via stochastic queuing: a key acts as a server, requests as customers, and the bucket as a finite waiting room. The veto condition is that these models fail when traffic exhibits long-range dependence (e.g., periodic bursts), requiring fractional Brownian motion extensions rather than Poisson.
